text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said state governments should consider setting up their own wildlife parks, adding that there should be a balance between development and protection of wildlife.
-- Malaysian Chinese Association president Ling Liong Sik said education will continue to be the emphasis of the party over the next 15 years.
-- Klang Valley folk are bracing themselves for massive traffic jams in and around the city today as almost everyone resumes work after the long "Kongsi-Raya" holidays.

-- The unit trust industry in Malaysia, while still in its infancy, is expected to make up about 10 percent of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange capitalisation by the year 2000 and 12.5 percent by 2005.

-- HongKong Bank Malaysia Bhd is embarking on a strategic plan of action for the next five years designed to enable it to retain its market share and enhance profitability in what it hopes will be a growing customer base.
